attempts.rationale: Test a basic robust combination (trend dominated, unstable ranking) – mean over all models.
test a weighted combination using inverse_error to exploit the ranking hint that a robust weighted mix may improve over mean.
The ranking is unstable (tau 0.15) and several correlated groups exist; a robust DBA may perform better than weighted.
test a per-horizon weighted scheme using softmax_neg_error to see if horizon-specific weighting improves over global weighted inverse_error.
Try a robust trimmed mean to reduce influence of high-error models, given unstable ranking and correlated groups.
The series is trend-dominated with unstable ranking; a robust median may outperform mean/weighted.
use per‑horizon one‑hot weighting to adapt to horizon‑specific model wins
The series has unstable ranking and several correlated groups; a forward-selection based weighting (w4) may pick a diverse subset that balances errors.
The series has unstable ranking (tau=0.15) and several correlated groups; a per‑horizon top‑k mean may capture complementary strengths across horizons.
The series is trend‑dominated with unstable ranking; a robust weighted mix over a small, diverse pool (pool4) might outperform full‑pool weighted.

The current leader uses a softmax-weighted mix on a small robust pool. A different kind of combination is to try a simple inverse-error weighting on the same pool, which may favor the top performers differently.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted on pool4 weighted by w8' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.8271. Series context: trend strength 0.8138 and seasonal strength 0.4153; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.15); 5 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 2.548.
